title: Small UTC clock bar at the bottom of the side panel, with local time
outcome: Greg sees the current UTC time, clearly labelled UTC, with his local time beside it, in a small unobtrusive bar at the bottom of the left side panel. Agents' UTC times can then be read without mental conversion. It changes no deadline rules.
acceptance: A small bar at the bottom of the side panel shows the current time clearly labelled UTC (HH:MM, 24-hour), plus the browser's local time and zone abbreviation (for example PST). It updates at minute boundaries, from one timer aligned to the next minute rather than a per-second render loop, and stops updating while the page is hidden.

A behavioural test with a controlled clock shows the rendered UTC and local text for a fixed instant, the change at the next minute boundary, and that no update is scheduled while the document is hidden.

The bar works at narrow, normal and wide panel sizes without covering or shifting the panel's filters and controls. It has an accessible text equivalent (for example a <time> element with a datetime attribute and an aria-label naming UTC). It is checked in the running UI on a real browser.
A clean review pair, a green full gate, and an independent acceptance evaluation.
